findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a cardinality guard to the proving command (e.g. `--collect-only -q` pre-check or `pytest ... -k resolver --co -q | grep -c 'test session'`) OR specify that test functions must be named with the `resolver` substring (e.g. `test_resolver_code_review`, `test_resolver_plan_review_parity`, `test_resolver_unknown_gate_key`) so the `-k resolver` filter is guaranteed to be non-vacuous.
evidence: Plan does not specify that test functions must include 'resolver' in their names
pytest exits 0 with 'no tests ran' when -k matches nothing, producing a false-green
findings.finding: The proving command `pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k resolver` will exit 0 with no tests run if no test functions happen to contain the substring 'resolver' in their names, because `-k` is a keyword filter and pytest does not error on zero matches by default. The plan specifies test behavior (happy path, parity, edge cases) but not the test function names, so an executor could name them `test_code_review_id`, `test_plan_review_parity`, etc. and the proving command would silently collect nothing.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — all three ACs reference `-k resolver`
scenarios: Executor names tests `test_happy_path`, `test_parity`, `test_unknown_key` — all three ACs show green with zero tests collected
CI passes the proving command without ever executing the assertions
findings.suggested_fix: In the AC text, either (a) name the three test functions explicitly — e.g. `test_resolver_code_review_gate`, `test_resolver_plan_review_default`, `test_resolver_unknown_gate_key` — and rely on those names satisfying `-k resolver`; or (b) replace the proving command with `pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` (no `-k` filter) and verify all three cases are covered by the file's full test suite, adding a comment that the file is dedicated to resolver tests.

findings.finding: The Testing section describes a cross-gate injectivity check ('no code-review project id collides with any plan-review physical id') but no Acceptance Criterion captures it, and all three ACs use the `-k resolver` pytest selector — so if the injectivity test is named differently, it is never exercised by any stated proving command.
findings.location: Testing section (edge case bullet) / Acceptance Criteria (all three ACs)
findings.suggested_fix:
Add to Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] No `code-review-*` physical id collides with any `plan-review-*` physical id for any valid criterion id; verified by `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'resolver or injectivity'`.

evidence: grep of `criterion_prompt_id` across the repo finds three callers: registry.py:302, criterion_preview.py:487, AND evals/eval.py:419
eval.py:419: `else criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)` — an unconditional no-gate-key call
Plan's Rejected Alternatives mentions eval.py:419 as the reason gate_key was not made required, but the Approach section's caller enumeration omits it
findings.finding: The plan asserts exactly 'two existing callers' of `criterion_prompt_id` (registry.py:302 and criterion_preview.py:487) that need no change, but a grep reveals a third existing caller at `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:419` that is not counted in this claim. The plan does acknowledge eval.py:419 in Rejected Alternatives, but the explicit count of 'two existing callers' in the Approach section is factually wrong. A reviewer auditing for completeness (e.g., confirming no call site is broken) would have an incomplete picture of the surface area from the Approach section alone.
findings.location: Approach section: 'The default `"plan_review"` preserves today's behavior byte-for-byte, so the two existing callers (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487`) need no change'
scenarios: A reviewer counting call sites from the Approach section only would conclude two sites need auditing, missing eval.py:419 — which would also silently resolve plan-review prompts for eval fixtures that may need the code-review namespace.
If a future change makes gate_key required (or a linter enforces explicit gate_key), eval.py:419 would be a surprise third breakage site not listed in scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'the two existing callers (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487`) need no change' to 'the three existing callers (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:419`) need no change — all produce plan-review prompt ids, which is correct for their current use cases.'

evidence: Plan states: 'the two existing callers (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302, src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487) need no change'
Grep result shows a third caller: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:414-419 imports and calls criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id) unconditionally

eval.py:416-419: prompt_id = (criterion_id if criterion_id.startswith('plan-review-') else criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)) — hardcoded 'plan-review-' string at line 418 is an additional behavioral quirk
Plan mentions eval.py:419 only in 'Rejected alternatives' to justify the default kwarg, never in the consumer/scope enumeration
findings.finding: The plan enumerates only two of the three existing callers of `criterion_prompt_id`, omitting `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:419`. That caller also contains a hardcoded `criterion_id.startswith("plan-review-")` guard at line 418 — a structural quirk that will interact with future code-review criterion IDs flowing through eval — which is never surfaced.
findings.location: Scope section / 'The two existing callers' claim
scenarios: A reviewer auditing blast radius will miss that eval.py is also a current consumer of the function being changed.
A future child ticket author adding gate_key='code_review' call sites may overlook that eval.py:418 also hard-codes the 'plan-review-' prefix guard, requiring a parallel fix there.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope section, extend the existing-callers sentence to: 'the three existing callers (registry.py:302, criterion_preview.py:487, evals/eval.py:419) need no change under the default; note that eval.py:418 also hard-codes a `startswith("plan-review-")` guard that a future code-review eval child must update to `startswith(("plan-review-", "code-review-"))` or equivalent.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Scope or Approach section, explicitly call out `eval.py:419` as a known-deferred seam (will resolve to wrong prefix for code-review project criteria until the eval-children ticket patches it with `gate_key="code_review"`), so child-ticket planners know to include it.
evidence: Plan: 'Making gate_key required — it would force editing eval.py:419's existing call… the default is the historically-correct value, not a silent bug.'

eval.py:416-419: 'prompt_id = (criterion_id if criterion_id.startswith("plan-review-") else criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id))' — no gate_key passed, always resolves to plan-review- prefix for non-prefixed ids.
Plan Scope lists only ids.py and the new test file; eval.py is not in scope but is an existing call site that will produce wrong output for code-review project criteria.
findings.finding: The plan asserts eval.py:419 'need[s] no change', but this existing call resolves criterion_prompt_id without gate_key. For plan-review criteria the default is correct; however, when code-review project criteria eventually flow through eval.py (the stated goal of the series), they will silently resolve to 'plan-review-project-<name>' instead of 'code-review-project-<name>' until the deferred 'eval children' ticket fixes this. The plan does not mark eval.py:419 as a known latent incorrect-resolution seam in Scope or Approach — only mentions it in the Rejected alternatives sidebar — so an implementer reading only Scope/Testing could conclude eval.py is fully handled.
scenarios: A developer runs `rebar prompt eval project.foo` for a code-review project criterion before the eval-children ticket lands; eval.py:419 silently loads plan-review-project-foo.eval.yaml (which may not exist or may be the wrong rubric), producing a confusing FileNotFoundError or incorrect eval results rather than a clear 'wrong gate_key' error.
An implementer reading only Scope + Testing sections concludes eval.py is already correct for code-review criteria and does not flag it as a known gap in the child ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Known deferred callers' note in Scope: 'eval.py:419 is intentionally left unchanged here — it uses the plan_review default and is correct for plan-review evals; the eval-admission child ticket must add gate_key="code_review" at this call site for code-review project criteria.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the leaf's `_PROMPT_PREFIX` private dict with the parent epic's explicit `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "code-review-"` naming: either expose a public `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` constant (in addition to or instead of the private dict) so the leaf satisfies the parent's stated deliverable, or update the parent epic's Scope to reflect the dict-based design before re-reviewing this leaf.
evidence: Leaf Approach: 'Introduce a `_PROMPT_PREFIX = {"plan_review": "plan-review-", "code_review": "code-review-"}` map in `ids.py`' — no public `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` constant is mentioned
Existing ids.py exposes `PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` as a named public module-level constant (line 31); the parent implies `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` is its symmetric counterpart

Seam children 761e, 8153, and 41e2 consume criterion_prompt_id with gate_key; if they also reference `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` directly (as the parent's naming implies), the missing symbol breaks their imports
findings.finding: The leaf delivers a private `_PROMPT_PREFIX` dict rather than the public `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` constant that the parent epic explicitly names as the ids.py deliverable. The parent scope reads 'Extend `criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id` with `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "code-review-"`', symmetrically matching the existing `PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` public constant. Downstream seam children that import `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` from `criteria.ids` by name will fail to find it if the leaf ships only the private dict.
findings.location: ## Approach (leaf plan) — `_PROMPT_PREFIX` dict; parent epic 119f ## Scope — `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "code-review-"`
scenarios: A downstream seam child does `from rebar.llm.criteria.ids import CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` — the symbol does not exist in the leaf's design, causing an ImportError.

A reviewer or author checks the parent's scope and expects to find `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX` as a public constant in ids.py after fc72 lands; it is absent, creating a divergence from the parent's contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX: str = "code-review-"` as a public module-level constant in ids.py alongside the private `_PROMPT_PREFIX` dict (or derive it from the dict: `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = _PROMPT_PREFIX["code_review"]`), mirroring the existing `PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX`. This satisfies the parent's explicit naming and keeps the private dict as the lookup mechanism.
